t: In the doctrine of precedent, the part of a judgment that is binding on subordinate courts is the:
o: obiter dicta
headnote prepared by the law reporter
dissenting opinion
ratio decidendi
e: The ratio decidendi is the legal principle on which the decision rests; obiter dicta are incidental remarks which carry persuasive value only.

t: The Insurance Act, 1938 came into force on:
o: 1 July 1939
26 January 1950
1 September 1956
1 April 1938
e: The Act was passed in 1938 and brought into force on 1 July 1939, replacing the Life Assurance Companies Act, 1912 and the Indian Insurance Companies Act, 1928.

t: A Permanent Lok Adalat for public utility services under Section 22A of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 can take up disputes relating to:
o: only criminal cases
insurance services, among other notified public utility services
only disputes between insurers and reinsurers
only matters already decided by a civil court
e: Insurance service is a notified public utility service, so a policyholder may approach the Permanent Lok Adalat before the dispute is brought before any court; it may decide on merits where settlement fails.

t: Section 100 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 provides that the Act's provisions are:
o: applicable only where no contract exists
the only remedy available to consumers
in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other law in force
subordinate to the Insurance Act, 1938
e: The consumer forum remedy is supplementary; a policyholder may alternatively pursue the Ombudsman, a civil suit or arbitration, though not simultaneously for the same cause.

t: Under Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a person is competent to contract if he:
o: is above 16 years and literate
is an Indian citizen of any age
has been assessed to income-tax
has attained majority, is of sound mind and is not disqualified by any law
e: The three conditions are majority, soundness of mind and absence of legal disqualification (for example, an alien enemy or an undischarged insolvent).

t: An 80-year-old bedridden widow, wholly dependent on her caretaker, is persuaded by him to assign her policy to him. Under Section 16 of the Indian Contract Act the assignment is most likely:
o: voidable on the ground of undue influence, since the caretaker was in a position to dominate her will
void for want of consideration
void for mistake of fact
valid, since it was signed voluntarily
e: Where one party is in a position to dominate the will of the other and obtains an unfair advantage, the presumption of undue influence arises and the transaction is voidable at her option.

t: A proposer honestly but wrongly states that his father died of a heart attack at 70, when he actually died at 55. This is an example of:
o: coercion under Section 15
misrepresentation under Section 18
fraud under Section 17
mistake of law under Section 21
e: A positive assertion that is untrue but believed to be true is misrepresentation; the contract is voidable, and under S.45 the insurer may act within three years if the fact was material.

t: The insurer informs the proposer that the risk is accepted subject to an extra premium of ₹2,000 per annum. In contract law this communication is:
o: a revocation of the proposal
an unconditional acceptance
a counter-offer, which the proposer accepts by paying the premium with the extra
an invitation to treat
e: Under S.7 an acceptance must be absolute and unqualified; acceptance on modified terms is a counter-offer which the proposer accepts by paying the loaded premium.

t: Which of the following agreements is NOT void under the Indian Contract Act, 1872?
o: An agreement in restraint of marriage of an adult
An agreement whose meaning is uncertain
A wagering agreement
An agreement to refer future disputes under a policy to arbitration
e: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings are void under S.28, but an arbitration agreement is expressly saved by Exception 1; wagers (S.30), restraint of marriage (S.26) and uncertain agreements (S.29) are void.

t: A sales brochure describing a life insurance plan and its premium rates issued by an insurer is, in contract law:
o: an acceptance
an invitation to offer
a counter-offer
an offer
e: The brochure merely invites proposals; the proposer's completed proposal form is the offer and the insurer remains free to accept, decline or modify it.

t: Section 2(h) of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 defines a contract as:
o: a proposal which has been accepted
an agreement enforceable by law
every promise forming consideration for each other
a set of reciprocal promises
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). A contract is an agreement enforceable by law; an agreement is every promise and set of promises forming consideration for each other (S.2(e)), and a promise is an accepted proposal (S.2(b)).

t: A wife proposes a policy on her husband's life. Which is correct about insurable interest?
o: Insurable interest exists only if the husband pays the premium
A wife cannot insure her husband's life under Indian law
Insurable interest between spouses is presumed and need not be proved
She must prove financial dependence on her husband
e: The law presumes insurable interest between husband and wife on grounds of natural affection, unlike relationships such as siblings where pecuniary interest must be shown.

t: A fact is 'material' for the purpose of disclosure in life insurance if:
o: the proposer personally considers it important
the agent asks a question about it
it is mentioned in the policy conditions
it would influence the judgment of a prudent insurer in deciding whether to accept the risk or on what terms
e: Materiality is judged objectively by the prudent-insurer test, not by the proposer's own view; Section 45 adds that the insurer must show the fact was material to the risk.

t: The life assured dies during the grace period with the renewal premium unpaid. The insurer will:
o: pay the claim after deducting the unpaid premium for the policy year
pay the premiums paid plus interest
pay only the surrender value
repudiate the claim because the premium was unpaid
e: Cover continues during the grace period; the policy is in force and the claim is payable, with the outstanding premium adjusted from the proceeds.

t: In a life insurance policy, proof of death and of the claimant's title are:
o: warranties given by the insurer
conditions precedent to the insurer's liability to pay
exclusions under the policy
optional formalities that can be waived by the agent
e: Payment is due only after the insurer receives satisfactory proof of the happening of the event and of who is entitled; an agent has no authority to waive policy conditions.

t: Within three years of issue, an insurer discovers that the proposer wrongly stated his monthly income as ₹60,000 instead of ₹55,000. Under Section 45(3) the insurer:
o: must repudiate and refund premiums
may reduce the sum assured proportionately
cannot repudiate unless it shows the misstatement was material to the risk
may repudiate because any misstatement is a ground
e: The proviso to S.45(3) bars repudiation for a misstatement that is not material; a small income variance would ordinarily not have changed the underwriting decision.

t: A 20-year non-linked endowment policy with sum assured ₹5,00,000 and annual premium ₹25,000 lapses after two full years' premiums. The reduced paid-up sum assured (excluding bonuses) is:
e: Paid-up sum assured = sum assured × premiums paid / premiums payable = 5,00,000 × 2/20 = ₹50,000, plus any vested bonuses.

topic: Group Life and Other Insurance Schemes
t: An employer's annual contribution to an approved gratuity fund (Part C of the Fourth Schedule to the Income-tax Act) is:
o: deductible as business expenditure under Section 36(1)(v)
not deductible at all
taxable in the hands of employees in the year of contribution
treated as the employer's income
e: Contributions to an approved gratuity fund, often funded through a group gratuity policy, are allowed as a deduction to the employer and are not taxed in employees' hands until gratuity is received.

t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024, a lapsed non-linked policy can be revived within:
o: two years from the date of the first unpaid premium
three years from the date of lapse
five years from the date of the first unpaid premium
one year from the end of the grace period
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The revival period is five years from the first unpaid premium, subject to the policy terms and evidence of continued insurability.

topic: Group Life and Other Insurance Schemes
t: The Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 presently applies to employees drawing wages up to:
o: ₹15,000 per month
₹25,000 per month
₹21,000 per month
₹10,000 per month
e: The wage ceiling for ESI coverage is ₹21,000 per month (₹25,000 for persons with disabilities); covered employees receive medical, sickness, maternity and dependants' benefits.

t: For an assignment of a life policy to be effective against the insurer, Section 38 requires that:
o: the assignee pays a transfer fee of 1% of the sum assured
the policy is reissued in the assignee's name
the assignment is approved by the agent
notice in writing of the assignment, with the instrument or its copy, is delivered to the insurer
e: The insurer is bound to recognise the assignment only from the date it receives notice; it records the assignment and issues an acknowledgement, and priority among competing assignees follows the order of notices.

t: A life insurance policy is an 'actionable claim' under Section 3 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, but its transfer is governed by:
o: Section 130 of the Transfer of Property Act only
the Indian Stamp Act, 1899
Section 38 of the Insurance Act, 1938, which is a special provision
the Registration Act, 1908
e: A policy is a right to money not in possession and hence an actionable claim, but the special procedure for assignment of policies in S.38 of the Insurance Act prevails over the general law.

t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024, a non-linked savings policy must acquire a surrender value:
o: only at the end of the policy term
only after five years' premiums
only after three years' premiums
after payment of the first full year's premium
e: The 2024 regulations require a special surrender value to be payable even where only one full year's premium has been paid, improving the position over the statutory two-year rule in S.113.

t: If the original policy document is lost, the policyholder can obtain a duplicate policy on:
o: furnishing an indemnity bond and, where required, an advertisement of loss
payment of a fresh first premium
surrendering the nomination
obtaining a court order
e: The policy bond is only evidence of the contract; insurers issue a duplicate after the policyholder indemnifies them against claims arising from the original, with an advertisement for larger sums.

t: The maximum aggregate deduction available under Section 80C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (including life insurance premiums) is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The overall ceiling under S.80C is ₹1.5 lakh per year under the old tax regime, covering life insurance premium, PPF, ELSS and other eligible items together.

t: A policyholder returns the policy within the free-look period stating that she disagrees with the terms. She is entitled to a refund of the premium paid:
o: in full without any deduction
less proportionate risk premium for the period on cover, medical examination expenses and stamp duty
less 50% as administrative charges
less the agent's commission only
e: The free-look provision allows cancellation with refund of premium, the insurer being permitted to deduct only the cost of cover for the period, medical costs and stamp duty charges.

t: A death certificate accepted as primary proof of death in a claim is issued under the:
o: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
Insurance Act, 1938
Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
Indian Succession Act, 1925
e: Deaths must be registered under the 1969 Act, and the certificate issued by the Registrar is the standard proof; insurers may require additional evidence in early or unnatural deaths.

t: Where an insurer is satisfied that policy money is payable but cannot determine which of several rival claimants is entitled, Section 47 of the Insurance Act permits it to:
o: pay the money to IRDAI
divide the money equally among all claimants
withhold payment indefinitely
pay the amount into the court having jurisdiction, obtaining a valid discharge
e: Payment into court under S.47 gives the insurer a complete discharge and leaves the rival claimants to establish their title before the court.

t: A life assured went missing in 2019 and has not been heard of since. In 2026 his wife lodges a death claim. Which statement is CORRECT?
o: The claim is payable automatically after seven years without any court order
The presumption of death arises after seven years, but insurers generally require a court declaration, and premiums must have been kept up in the meantime
The policy automatically becomes paid-up from the date of disappearance
The presumption of death arises after three years of disappearance
e: The seven-year presumption does not fix the date of death; insurers therefore ask for a court decree and require premiums to be paid to keep the policy in force until death is presumed.

t: Contributions to an annuity plan of an insurer are deductible under Section 80CCC subject to:
o: no monetary limit
a separate limit of ₹1 lakh
the overall ceiling of ₹1.5 lakh shared with Section 80C and 80CCD(1)
a limit of 10% of salary
e: Section 80CCE caps the combined deduction under 80C, 80CCC and 80CCD(1) at ₹1.5 lakh; the pension received later is taxable as income.

t: A policy issued in 2010 has a sum assured of ₹2,00,000 and an annual premium of ₹35,000. The premium eligible for deduction under Section 80C is:
e: For policies issued before 1 April 2012 the limit is 20% of the sum assured, i.e. ₹40,000; since the premium of ₹35,000 is within this, the whole premium qualifies.

t: On retirement an employee commutes part of his pension from an approved superannuation fund and also receives gratuity. The commuted pension is exempt under Section 10(10A) to the extent of:
o: one-third of the pension he would otherwise have received
the full commuted amount
one-half of the pension he would otherwise have received
₹20 lakh
e: Where gratuity is received, one-third of the commuted value is exempt; where no gratuity is received the exemption is one-half. The uncommuted pension is taxed as salary.

t: The minimum educational qualification prescribed for appointment as an individual insurance agent is:
o: pass in Class XII
pass in Class X (or equivalent)
a graduate degree
a diploma in insurance
e: The agent regulations require at least a Class X pass, besides clearing the prescribed examination conducted by the examination body approved by IRDAI.

t: Unlike an insurance agent, an insurance broker:
o: cannot deal with more than one insurer
represents the insurer only
represents the client and owes duties to the client, though remunerated by the insurer
can underwrite risks on behalf of the insurer
e: A broker is the agent of the insured who arranges cover with any insurer; an insurance agent acts for a particular insurer.

t: A 'Point of Sales Person' (POSP) under IRDAI guidelines is permitted to:
o: sell any life insurance product including ULIPs
act as a broker for corporate clients
underwrite group policies
solicit only simple, pre-underwritten products specified by IRDAI
e: POSPs undergo minimal training and can sell only standardised products that need no underwriting judgement, such as pure term and simple savings plans within set limits.

t: While a minor's own agreement is void, a life insurance policy on a minor's life is valid because:
o: the contract is made by the parent or guardian having insurable interest, with the minor as life assured
the Insurance Act exempts minors from the Contract Act
the insurer waives the requirement of competency
a minor is competent to contract after 16
e: The proposer, not the minor, is the party to the contract; the minor is only the life assured and the policy vests in him on majority.

t: A company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 can take a keyman policy on its director because a company:
o: is the same as its shareholders
is a separate legal person capable of contracting in its own name
needs no insurable interest
is treated as a minor in law
e: A company is an artificial juristic person with perpetual succession; it contracts through its board and has insurable interest in persons whose loss would affect its profits.

t: In a life insurance contract, insurable interest must exist:
o: At the time of the claim only
At inception of the policy
Both at inception and at claim
At renewal each year
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Life: at inception only. Marine: at the time of loss. Fire and motor: at both inception and loss.

t: The initial capital provided by the Central Government to the Life Insurance Corporation of India under the LIC Act, 1956 was:
o: ₹1 crore
₹100 crore
₹5 crore
₹50 crore
e: LIC was set up with a capital of ₹5 crore wholly provided by the Government; its paid-up capital was raised and the Corporation was listed in 2022.

t: The exclusive privilege of LIC to carry on life insurance business in India under Section 30 of the LIC Act, 1956 was ended by:
o: a notification of the Reserve Bank of India
the Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2021
the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act, 2015
the IRDA Act, 1999, through its schedule amending the LIC Act
e: The Third Schedule to the IRDA Act, 1999 amended S.30 to permit any registered Indian insurance company to transact life business, ending the monopoly.

t: The number of Insurance Ombudsman centres in India is at present:
e: There are 17 Ombudsman offices across the country, each with territorial jurisdiction, administered by the Council for Insurance Ombudsmen.

t: 'Bima Bharosa' is:
o: a government-sponsored crop insurance scheme
IRDAI's online integrated grievance management portal for policyholders
the name of the Insurance Ombudsman's website
an IRDAI consumer awareness magazine
e: The Integrated Grievance Management System (IGMS) was rebranded as Bima Bharosa in 2022; it lets policyholders register and track complaints escalated beyond the insurer.

t: An appeal against an order of a District Commission lies to the State Commission within:
o: 60 days from the date of the order
90 days from the date of the order
45 days from the date of the order
30 days from the date of the order
e: Section 41 of the CPA, 2019 prescribes 45 days (condonable for sufficient cause); appeals from the State to the National Commission lie within 30 days.

t: Which of the following disputes is OUTSIDE the jurisdiction of the Insurance Ombudsman?
o: Partial or total repudiation of a claim by an insurer
Delay in settlement of a claim beyond the period specified by IRDAI
Misrepresentation of policy terms at the time of sale
A dispute between an insurer and its agent regarding commission
e: The Ombudsman handles complaints of policyholders, nominees and legal heirs against insurers; intermediary disputes with insurers are not covered.

t: Section 64VA of the Insurance Act, 1938 requires every insurer to maintain:
o: an excess of the value of its assets over its liabilities of not less than the required solvency margin
a reserve fund equal to one year's premium
a deposit of ₹10 crore with the RBI
reinsurance of 20% of every policy
e: The solvency margin provision ensures insurers have a cushion over liabilities; IRDAI regulations prescribe the method and the control level of 150%.

t: Non-disclosure of a material fact by the proposer makes the contract:
o: Void ab initio
Voidable at the option of the insurer
Illegal
Automatically continued on revised terms
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Breach of utmost good faith renders the contract voidable, not void; the insurer may elect to avoid it (subject to Section 45 for life).

t: Section 41 of the Insurance Act, 1938 prohibits:
o: assignment of policies to banks
offering any rebate of premium or commission as an inducement to take out or renew a policy
insuring the lives of persons above 65
paying commission to an agent
e: Rebating distorts fair competition and underwriting; both the person offering and the person accepting a rebate commit an offence punishable with a penalty up to ₹10 lakh.

t: Which statement about Section 64VB of the Insurance Act is INCORRECT?
o: Where premium is paid by cheque, the risk is assumed only on realisation of the cheque, except as the Rules provide
Group policies enjoy exceptions prescribed under the Insurance Rules
An agent may assume risk on the insurer's behalf before premium is received if he issues a receipt
No risk may be assumed unless the premium is received in advance
e: An agent has no authority to bind the insurer to a risk; the prohibition applies to the insurer and risk begins only after premium is received or guaranteed in the prescribed manner.

topic: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999
t: Which of the following is a function of IRDAI under Section 14 of the IRDA Act, 1999?
o: Fixing the income-tax treatment of insurance proceeds
Appointing the Insurance Ombudsman
Conducting the business of reinsurance
Specifying the qualifications, code of conduct and practical training for intermediaries and agents
e: Section 14 lists IRDAI's powers: registration of insurers, protection of policyholders, qualifications and conduct of agents and intermediaries, solvency, investments and adjudication of insurer-intermediary disputes.

topic: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999
t: The Chairperson of IRDAI holds office for a term of:
o: five years, or until attaining the age of 65, whichever is earlier
five years, or until attaining the age of 62
six years, with no age limit
three years, or until attaining the age of 60
e: Section 5 fixes five years or age 65 for the Chairperson; whole-time members serve five years or until 62, and all are eligible for reappointment.
